topics.label: Lecture overview and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure and outlines the key learning objectives regarding cancer etiology, environmental exposures, and carcinogenicity testing.

topics.label: Intrinsic and extrinsic factors in cancer etiology and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational causes of cancer, balancing endogenous replicative errors and genetic predisposition against environmental exposures supported by geographic and migrant epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens and cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how biological agents such as viruses, bacteria, and parasites contribute to oncogenesis, focusing on their mechanisms and the specific etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical carcinogens, metabolic activation, and DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine dietary, environmental, and occupational mutagens—such as aflatoxin, UV light, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and aromatic amines—and how host metabolic processing mediates their DNA-damaging effects.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and developmental timing
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, focusing on how chronic inflammation, chemical promoters in two-stage models, and periods of high tissue proliferation facilitate tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and assessing cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro testing strategies used to establish carcinogenicity and evaluate dose-dependent cancer risks.
